- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion periods; if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to capture rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; reduce first 3–5 days by 0.5–1.0%.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often misses the pivot; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% in the following 3–5 days.
